parties.name: Together (B'Yachad)
parties.summary: The strongest offer on Daniel's everyday issues: a detailed cost-of-living plan with import liberalisation, a large long-term rental programme and the only landlord incentive for longer leases. It still has nothing on retaliatory eviction, agent fees or enforcement, and Bennett's annexation stance and the 'replace Netanyahu' framing sit poorly with him.

why.A1: Not supply-only: tax benefits for private landlords on 5+ year leases and 'long-term certainty for tenants', plus 100k long-term rental units (40% regulated, 30% below market). Nothing on eviction, retaliation, agent fees or enforcement. Lapid/German co-sponsored the 2017 Fair Rental Law
why.A2: Concrete: 100k long-term rental units in 10 years, lease-purchase after 10 years, urban-renewal and permit timelines. Benefits skewed to reservists; no curbs on investment-only stock
why.A3: Most specific A3 plan of any list: food prices -30% in 3 years, lower import barriers, gradual tariff cuts, break importer monopolies, accept international kosher certification, OECD-average basket target
why.A4: Plan pages exist on health, transport, small businesses and public service, but the evidence file did not read them
why.A5: Ending regional isolation through alliances; no explicit plan to repair reputation through conduct
why.A6: About 25 web plan pages in Hebrew, English, Russian and Amharic, with some numeric targets; PM term limit and a constitution proposal. No PDF, not costed, no consultation; identity partly 'replace Netanyahu'
why.B1: Mandatory conscription; no state funding for those who don't serve, work or study the core curriculum
why.B2: Regulate Basic Laws and the judiciary 'through broad consensus', constitution proposal: not a pledge to repeal the overhaul
why.B3: Replacing Netanyahu is the list's core purpose
why.B4: Anti-Netanyahu bloc; no explicit ruling-out of Ben-Gvir/Smotrich read
why.B5: Bennett favours annexing Area C and rejects statehood; Lapid's separation line is subordinate. Joint position unclear
why.B6: Strong security plus regional alliances
why.B7: Bennett backs Shabbat public transport and civil marriage; religion-and-state plan page
why.B8: State commission as the government's first act: Daniel supports one but not as front-line policy
why.B9: Diaspora/aliyah plan pages exist but were not read; no spending position

parties.name: The Democrats
parties.summary: The best match on documentation and on almost every Stream B position, with the only substantive plan on Israel's reputation. On rent, its top issue for Daniel, it diagnoses the problem but offers only more long-term rental and public housing, and it leans on price controls rather than competition.

why.A1: Names 'rent that shatters dreams' but the only remedy is to expand long-term rental and affordable public housing: supply-only, no numbers. Meretz's Zandberg co-sponsored the 2017 Fair Rental Law
why.A2: Dense planning near transport, urban renewal, varied unit sizes, expanded affordable public housing; resident-aimed but no numbers
why.A3: Fight food, drug and energy cartels, cut transport fares and out-of-pocket costs; but widens price controls and says nothing on imports
why.A4: Broad: health, welfare, education, public transport, north/south rehabilitation, digital access to justice, more judges. Thin on bureaucracy and civil defence
why.A5: Says Israel is seen as extreme and isolated; proposes a regional initiative with the US and moderate Arab states, Saudi normalisation, IMEC: repair through policy
why.A6: Full 16-page platform PDF (Aug 2026), structured 'five steps per theme'; site in English, Arabic, Russian, Spanish, though the PDF is Hebrew-only. PM term limit, no indicted ministers. Not costed, no consultation
why.B1: Absolute equality of burden, national service for all, stop funding Haredi education networks; not the lead message
why.B2: Repeal all 'regime coup' laws including the judges' committee law
why.B3: Blames Netanyahu governments; 'no indicted PM'; firmly in the opposition bloc
why.B4: Campaigns against 'the most extreme and religious government in Israel's history'
why.B5: Two states, halt annexation, PA role in Gaza: further than Daniel's 'can't see how', but he does not rule it out in principle
why.B6: Strong military plus regional initiative, Iran isolation
why.B7: Civil marriage and divorce, end Rabbinate monopolies, Shabbat transport, fight religious coercion
why.B8: State commission, implement conclusions; not the lead item
why.B9: Platform PDF silent on diaspora and hasbara

why.A1: Supply-side rental: 20k long-term rental units a year, rent-to-buy saving 30% of rent; Malinovsky bill for a renter tax credit. No lease or eviction protection
why.A2: Land tenders on build quality not land price, 90% mortgages to 40 years for young couples, rent-to-own; partly service-linked

findings:
**Bottom line.** On the rubric built from my voice note, the best match among lists polling above the threshold is **Together (Bennett–Lapid), ballot letters רק**, followed by **The Democrats (אמת)** and **Yisrael Beiteinu (ל)**. The order of the top three is the same on Stream A alone, at 70/30 and at 50/50. Fourth and fifth (Joint List, Yashar) swap places at 50/50.

**The headline finding is a gap.** No list on the ballot has a real tenant-protection policy, my top issue. The best A1 score is 3 out of 5 (Together, for tax incentives on leases of five years or more). Nobody proposes limits on no-cause or retaliatory eviction, enforcement of repair duties, or enforcement of the agent-fee ban. That is what I suspected in the note (07:25): "not a single major party … had bothered to articulate any serious policy for" it. It is still true on election day.

The top five, with reasons:

1. **Together (רק): 71.5.** The strongest Stream A offer: the most detailed cost-of-living plan (import and tariff liberalisation with price targets), 100,000 long-term rental units, and the only measure aimed at lease length. Weaker on Stream B than the Democrats (Bennett's annexation stance), and its identity is partly "replace Netanyahu".
2. **The Democrats (אמת): 63.5.** The closest match on almost every Stream B issue, the best-documented programme (a 16-page platform PDF), and the only real plan on Israel's reputation. On rent it diagnoses the problem but offers only more public and long-term rental housing. On prices it leans on price controls rather than competition.
3. **Yisrael Beiteinu (ל): 54.0.** Concrete rental-supply and mortgage numbers, and strong on competition (ending exclusive importers) and on religion and state. Nothing on tenant protection, services or reputation, and it leads with the Haredi draft, the framing I call "the same story".
4. **Joint List (ודם): 46.8.** The only rent cap of any major list (20% of household income) and a published socio-economic programme. Its trade protectionism and its security positions are far from mine.
5. **Yashar (דרך): 46.5.** Polls second overall and fits me on Stream B, but on everyday issues it offers one undetailed phrase on renters. It leads with the October 7 commission and its leader's name: the ex-general's party pattern from the note.

Lists running Netanyahu for PM, or pledged to recommend only him, are excluded by my stated choice (Likud, Shas, Otzma Yehudit, RZP–Zehut, Noam, Amcha Yisrael). The best match below the threshold is the Reservists and the Economic Party (about 2 seats in recent polls).

These are judgements against my own stated positions, made by AI agents from public evidence gathered on election day. They are not a neutral rating of the parties. Every score has a written reason in the party profiles and in `data/scores.json`.
